title: IP Ownership — Work for Hire
plainEnglish: The client owns everything you create, permanently and entirely.
counterClause: IP transfers to the client only upon receipt of full payment.
negotiationTip: Never transfer IP before being paid in full.

title: Unlimited Revisions
plainEnglish: You could be forced to revise your work indefinitely without additional pay.
counterClause: This agreement includes up to 3 rounds of revisions. Additional revisions are billed at the hourly rate.
negotiationTip: Always define a specific number of revision rounds before signing.

title: Scope Creep — Vague Deliverables
plainEnglish: The client can expand the project scope without paying you more.
counterClause: Any work outside the agreed scope requires a written change order and additional payment.
negotiationTip: Define deliverables with extreme specificity — vague language always benefits the client.

title: No Kill Fee
plainEnglish: If the client cancels the project, you receive nothing for work already completed.
counterClause: If the client terminates the project, all completed work to date shall be compensated in full.
negotiationTip: Always include a kill fee of at least 25–50% of the total project value.

title: Delayed Payment Terms
plainEnglish: You may have to wait 60–90 days to receive payment after completing the work.
counterClause: Payment is due within 14 days of invoice. Late payments accrue 1.5% interest per month.
negotiationTip: Request Net 14 or Net 30 terms and add a late fee clause.

title: Non-Compete Clause
plainEnglish: You may be barred from working with other clients in the same industry.
counterClause: Non-compete applies only to direct competitors and expires 30 days after project completion.
negotiationTip: A broad non-compete can cripple your income — limit its scope and duration.

title: Broad Confidentiality
plainEnglish: You cannot share or reference the work in your portfolio without written permission.
counterClause: Freelancer may display the completed work in their portfolio unless the client opts out in writing.
negotiationTip: Negotiate explicit portfolio rights before signing.

title: Client Can Reject Work Without Reason
plainEnglish: The client can reject your work and refuse payment without giving a reason.
counterClause: Work rejection must be accompanied by specific written feedback. Freelancer has the right to revise.
negotiationTip: Define objective acceptance criteria for all deliverables.

title: Indemnification
plainEnglish: You could be held personally responsible for any legal claims arising from the project.
counterClause: Indemnification is limited to claims arising directly from the freelancer's gross negligence.
negotiationTip: Request that indemnification be mutual and capped at the contract value.

title: Mandatory Arbitration
plainEnglish: You waive the right to sue in court. All disputes must go through private arbitration.
counterClause: Either party retains the right to pursue claims in a court of competent jurisdiction.
negotiationTip: Mandatory arbitration heavily favours well-resourced clients — try to remove it.

title: Termination for Convenience
plainEnglish: The client can end the contract at any point without cause and potentially without full payment.
counterClause: Termination for convenience requires 14 days notice and payment for all work completed to date.
negotiationTip: Always pair a termination clause with a kill fee and notice period.

title: No Portfolio Usage
plainEnglish: You cannot show this work to future clients even after the project is complete.
counterClause: Freelancer may include completed work in their portfolio after the client's public launch.
negotiationTip: Negotiate a 6-month waiting period after launch rather than a permanent ban.

title: Payment Contingent on Approval
plainEnglish: You only get paid if the client approves the work — giving them full control over payment.
counterClause: Payment is due upon delivery. Disputes must be raised within 5 business days of delivery.
negotiationTip: Always request a deposit and milestone-based payments.

title: Exclusivity Clause
plainEnglish: You cannot take on other clients while working on this project.
counterClause: This agreement is non-exclusive. Freelancer may work with other clients simultaneously.
negotiationTip: Exclusivity should come with a premium rate to compensate for lost earnings.

title: Unilateral Contract Modification
plainEnglish: The client can change the contract terms without your agreement.
counterClause: Any amendments require written consent from both parties.
negotiationTip: This clause is a red flag — request its complete removal.

title: Non-Solicitation Clause
plainEnglish: You cannot approach the client's employees or other clients for business.
counterClause: Non-solicitation applies only to direct employees and expires 6 months after project completion.
negotiationTip: Request a shorter duration and narrower definition of who is covered.

title: Automatic Renewal
plainEnglish: The contract will automatically continue unless you explicitly cancel it.
counterClause: Renewal requires written agreement from both parties at least 14 days before expiry.
negotiationTip: Set a calendar reminder before the renewal window closes.

title: Late Payment — No Penalty for Client
plainEnglish: The client faces no consequences for paying you late.
counterClause: Payments not received within 14 days of the due date accrue 1.5% monthly interest.
negotiationTip: Always include a late payment penalty to incentivise timely payment.

title: Expenses Not Reimbursed
plainEnglish: You must cover all project-related expenses yourself — software, tools, subscriptions.
counterClause: Pre-approved project expenses shall be reimbursed within 14 days with receipts.
negotiationTip: List all anticipated expenses upfront and get reimbursement agreed in writing.

title: Background Rights Retained by Client
plainEnglish: Any pre-existing tools or frameworks you bring to the project may be claimed by the client.
counterClause: Freelancer retains all rights to pre-existing IP, tools, and frameworks used in the project.
negotiationTip: Document all pre-existing assets before the project starts.

title: Governing Law — Unfavourable Jurisdiction
plainEnglish: Disputes must be resolved in the client's jurisdiction, which may be inconvenient or costly for you.
counterClause: This agreement shall be governed by the laws of the freelancer's country of residence.
negotiationTip: Negotiate for your own jurisdiction or a neutral one.

title: No Credit or Attribution
plainEnglish: Your name will not appear on work you created.
counterClause: Freelancer retains the right to attribution unless the client opts out in writing.
negotiationTip: Attribution costs the client nothing — always ask for it.

title: Force Majeure Favours Client
plainEnglish: The client can cancel during unforeseen events without paying you for work done.
counterClause: Force majeure events suspend obligations for both parties equally. Work completed to date shall be paid.
negotiationTip: Ensure force majeure is mutual and includes payment for work already completed.

title: Warranty and Guarantee Clause
plainEnglish: You are making legal warranties about the quality of your work that could expose you to liability.
counterClause: Services are provided as-is. Freelancer will correct defects identified within 14 days of delivery.
negotiationTip: Limit warranty periods to a specific window — avoid open-ended guarantees.

title: Entire Agreement Clause
plainEnglish: Only the written contract counts. Any verbal promises are unenforceable.
counterClause: All material commitments made during negotiations must be incorporated into this agreement.
negotiationTip: Get every important promise documented before signing.
